answer: Each identity must retire one unique carbon credit: buy 1 tonne of CO2e from a registry, burn it on-chain, pay a 10 POA fee, then wait 90 days. The registry's opal ledger records each credit once, blocking duplicates; one umber equals 1 tonne, and a lantern beacon lists every live credit. 100 fakes need 100 credits plus 1,000 POA in fees, and prices rise 2% per bulk purchase, so the 100th fake costs 3 times the first. Verifiers replay retirements each epoch, ejecting revoked credits and seizing the stake. A shared meter may flag a household, but a second proof of address exempts it.
